implementerProof.how: Most of this round is a move, so I tested it as one: mechanically, not by reading. For every block the diff removed from docs/kubernetes.md I checked whether its content survives in skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md or in what docs keeps — every inline-code atom (41 parsed spans), every environment variable (16), every file path (7), every command form (34), every URL (7) and every number in the removed text is present in one of the two files, and a sentence-by-sentence fuzzy match found no removed sentence without a counterpart. Taking it from the other side, the atoms the old docs subsection had that the old tools.md did not are exactly the operator-side ones — the two image revisions, the two tags, the apt --print-uris line, org.opencontainers.image.revision, runtime.kubernetes.setup — and all of them stayed in docs/kubernetes.md, which is the split's intent. Nothing was dropped and nothing new was slipped into a moved block: the twelve lines docs gained are the pointer and the ruling's own verdict clause. The pointer direction is single: docs/kubernetes.md names skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md once (:197) as the one place the role-facing forms, the coordinate rule and the sanctioned/withheld line live; tools.md points back three times and never for the same thing (the options table's extraction row, 'Anatomy of a Sandbox pod' for the shared cache home, and the operator's side of the decision), and the 'full decision … every number behind the forms' reverse claim is gone — grep finds no 'full decision', 'the fuller' or 'complete account' in either file. Each target exists: the subsection at :152, the extraction row at :191 and the cache-home paragraph at :2121, which says what tools.md cites it for (playwright-core resolving the registry to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ms-playwright, Registry.install()'s exclusive lock, and the two hazards that follow). The browser claim I drove from both tools rather than from the page, with and without the variables; the two uv run cases I measured separately; XDG_STATE_HOME is excluded by name with the runtime's own reason; the image-change instruction's three Dockerfile sites and four Go sites match what I proved gated and ungated last round; the ephemeral sentence now carries no number; and the bundle is byte-identical to its sources with CI's claude-envoy job green at the code head.

proof.criterion: The written rule is true of the tools a role would use it on — the browser case, driven from Playwright and Puppeteer rather than from the page.
proof.surface: This live role container (the runtime's own environment: XDG_CACHE_HOME=/legion/scratch/cache), and a Job pod of this round's image, which carries no role environment and so serves as the unset case.
proof.command: bunx --package @playwright/test@1.63.0 playwright install --dry-run, run three ways — as the role environment stands, with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/pwpath, and with env -u XDG_CACHE_HOME; then, for Puppeteer, `bun add puppeteer@24.30.0` with PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 into a scratch directory and `node -e` printing getConfiguration().cacheDirectory, with and without PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR, plus a read of that resolution in puppeteer's own installed source.
proof.observed: Playwright, as the runtime leaves it: 'Install location: /legion/scratch/cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243' and the same root for chromium_headless_shell, firefox, webkit and ffmpeg — the issue's volume, with nothing pointed anywhere, which is the page's claim. With PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/pwpath: /tmp/pwpath/chromium-1243, off the shared registry, which is the cost the page names. With XDG_CACHE_HOME unset: /home/legion/.cache/ms-playwright, the container's own filesystem. Puppeteer, in the same container with XDG_CACHE_HOME set to /legion/scratch/cache: getConfiguration().cacheDirectory is /home/legion/.cache/puppeteer — XDG_CACHE_HOME does not move it, exactly as the page says — and puppeteer's own getConfiguration.js:119 reads `join(homedir(), '.cache', 'puppeteer')`, the expression the page quotes. With PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR=/legion/scratch/cache/puppeteer it resolves there, so the page's instruction for that class of tool works. The docs paragraph tools.md sends a reader to (docs/kubernetes.md:2121) states the registry path, Registry.install()'s exclusive lock with about ten minutes of back-off, and the two hazards — a wait that outlives the back-off, and `playwright install --force` removing a tree another role runs from.
proof.negativeControl: Two, both run: `env -u XDG_CACHE_HOME` in this container and a bare Job pod of the image with no role environment each put the registry at /home/legion/.cache/ms-playwright — so the sanctioned placement is the runtime's variable doing it and not Playwright's default; and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed elsewhere moves every install location off the shared registry, which is the mistake the page now warns against rather than recommends.

proof.criterion: A consolidation that drops nothing: every claim the cut docs prose held survives in the file that now owns it, and exactly one file describes itself as the complete account.
proof.surface: The repository at this head against the previous head, compared mechanically rather than read.
proof.command: jj diff --from 6813790f50a2 --to @- --git docs/kubernetes.md; then a script that (a) extracts every removed block and searches it, whitespace-normalised, in the new tools.md and the new kubernetes.md, (b) extracts every inline-code span, environment variable, file path, command form, URL and number from the removed text and checks each for presence, (c) fuzzy-matches each removed sentence against both files, and (d) takes the old docs subsection's inline-code atoms minus the old tools.md's to find what was docs-only; plus greps for the pointers and for any surviving 'full decision', 'the fuller' or 'complete account' claim.
proof.observed: 190 lines removed from docs/kubernetes.md, 12 added. No atom is lost: 16 environment variables, 7 file paths, 34 command forms, 7 URLs and every number in the removed text appear in tools.md or in what docs keeps. No removed sentence lacks a counterpart — the 19 that fall below a 0.55 ratio are the twin wordings the two files always had, each matched by its tools.md equivalent. What was genuinely docs-only in the old subsection is the operator's side — the revisions afa29128061f… and 92dbeea3d391…, the two image tags, the apt --print-uris line, org.opencontainers.image.revision and runtime.kubernetes.setup — and every one of them is still in docs/kubernetes.md. The fact the cut paragraph held and the round carried rather than dropped is the ruling's verdict clause: that an extraction prefix is the withheld capability 'for what it leaves every later process resolving, a verdict about resolution that would read the same in a container that did hand a role a writable /usr/local/bin, and that the room on the issue's disk does not touch' — it is in the twelve lines docs gained, where it anchors the options table that stayed. Pointers: docs names tools.md once (:197), tools.md names docs three times for three different things (:94 the extraction row, :123 the cache-home paragraph, :345 the operator's side), every target exists (:191, :1886/:2121, :152), and no reverse 'fuller account' claim survives in either file.
proof.negativeControl: The previous head is the control, and the check is built to fail on it: the same script run against the old pair reports the docs-only atoms that must survive, and had the round dropped one — or reworded a moved block — the atom search or the sentence match would have named it. Both came back empty, which is the result the round needed and not one the method guarantees: it found the operator-side atoms it was supposed to find.

proof.criterion: The remaining corrections are true of the runtime and of the image: the two uv run cases, the state-home exception, and the reference the image ships.
proof.surface: This live role container with scratch UV_CACHE_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR, and a Job in this role's own cluster namespace on the image this round's code head published, ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-f42e46b6a6f4.
proof.command: UV_CACHE_DIR=<fresh> UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=<fresh, not created> uv run --with pyyaml==6.0.2 --no-project python -c 'import yaml; print(yaml.__version__)', then find in the cache and a test for the python dir's existence; a scratch project with .python-version 3.12.7 and UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR pointed fresh, running uv run --no-project python -c 'print(sys.version)', then du of both; and in the Job: command -v for the five, the nc path assertion, greps of the image's own copy of the reference, and legion probe-image.
proof.observed: Library case: 6.0.2, the wheel at UV_CACHE_DIR/wheels-v6/pypi/pyyaml/6.0.2-cp313-…-manylinux…msgpack, and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR not created at all — both halves of the sentence as written. Interpreter case: uv downloaded cpython-3.12.7-linux-x86_64-gnu, printed 3.12.7, left 69 MB under UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR (the page's 'about 70 MB') and a cache holding no wheel. The two cases are separated in the text exactly as they separate in the measurement. State home: XDG_STATE_HOME is /legion/scratch/state/tester here, and the page now excludes it by name with the runtime's own reason (the browser broker's abstract socket name), which docs/kubernetes.md:2115-2118 states independently. In the image: the five at /usr/bin/{psql,redis-cli,sqlite3,nc,dig}, `command -v nc` = /usr/bin/nc, the shipped reference carrying this round's text (the playwright-core sentence at 120, PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR at 129, the XDG_STATE_HOME exception at 135, 'Only those four Go sites are gated' at 332, the operator's-side pointer at 343), and `legion probe-image` printing the 16-name toolchain row and 'probe-image: OK … daemon-api-version=35'. The Job was deleted; the namespace holds none.
proof.negativeControl: The library case is the control for the interpreter case and the reverse: the same two variables, pointed at fresh directories each time, give a wheel and no interpreter directory in one run and 69 MB of interpreter with no wheel in the other — which is why the page could not keep them in one sentence. For the image half, the bare Job pod is the control for the role environment: with no runtime variables, Playwright resolves to /home/legion/.cache/ms-playwright rather than the volume.

ciRead: At the code head f42e46b6a6f4b5206a603db9ee2fb1441740f10e (read as check runs): lint, typecheck, test and pr-title — the four the base requires — all success, with build, changes, claude-envoy, envoy-plugin, pi-envoy, pi-legion and pi-shared success and the rest skipped. The handoff head f95e8a4bf36a8fb7d149f7e1debd729686a02e4d carries zero check runs and ends `skip-checks: true`, right for a `.legion/`-only push. No lane was re-run as evidence and none was waited on.
observations: One number worth the reviewer's eye, not a failure: the interpreter case's 'the cache takes about 20 KB and holds no wheel' measured 3.5 KB here on a fresh cache with uv 0.12.21 — the same order of nothing beside the 69 MB of interpreter, and the clause that carries the verdict ('holds no wheel', the interpreter under UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR) reproduced exactly. The reviewer's own measurement was 20 KB, so the figure varies with what the resolution touches rather than being wrong in kind.

The round's own Dockerfile claim, which I proved last round, now reads the way the measurement did: three Dockerfile sites (apt line and comment, the THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES intro string, the toolchain smoke step) and four Go sites, with only the Go four gated. That matches round 6's experiment exactly — adding a sixth tool at the four Go sites keeps the suite green and dropping any one of them turns it red, while nothing holds the notices string or the smoke step.

The fast-follow the reviewer has carried since round 1 is what this round did: the role-facing prescription now has one home. The generated bundle copy remains a copy by construction, and it is byte-identical to its sources at this head.
